How do Backend Policy Hardening, Session Governance, and Next.js 16 MVVM Lock SCRIPE Auth End-to-End?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE secures Admin and User authentication across three coupled layers: $s2$ cryptographic credential validation with non-auto-login recovery, unified ISessionIssuerService session ceilings and instant revocation, and fail-closed Next.js 16 Edge and RouteGuard MVVM boundaries.

  1. Pre-auth login, workspace discovery, password reset, and WebAuthn handlers reject invalid encrypted tenant IDs (422) and filter .IgnoreQueryFilters() queries explicitly by active and non-deleted flags.
  2. Recovery splits verification (POST /verify-reset-otp issuing a single-use ResetGrantToken) from mutation (POST /reset-password returning 204 No Content) so password resets never auto-issue session tokens.
  3. Every password, SSO, SAML, magic-link, passkey, and OTP channel converges on ISessionIssuerService, ordering HybridMfaPolicy before MustChangePassword (mcp=true) and RequireMfaEnrollment (mfa_enroll=true).
  4. Frontend auth keeps Bearer JWTs in memory (useAppStore), deletes defaultRedirectPath persistence, exempts recovery routes, and gates SignalR & navigation until mcp and mfa_enroll are cleared.

Applies toSCRIPE-Backend + SCRIPE-Frontend + SCRIPE-CLIVerified

1

Which Auth, Policy, and Governance Thresholds Govern Runtime Behavior?

Six bounded numeric thresholds control brute-force resistance, password reuse prevention, OTP exhaustion, and JWT/session windows across tenants (sources: JwtOptions.cs, TenantSettings.cs, VerificationSettings.cs, SessionIssuerService.PolicyHelpers.cs).

Default Access JWT Lifetime

30min / 60min

30 / 60

JwtOptions.ExpiryMinutes = 30 fallback when SessionPolicy leaves AccessTokenExpiryMinutes unset; impersonation refresh caps at 8h.

Default Lockout Threshold

5fails / 5fails

5 / 5

LoginLockoutThreshold = 5 locks Admin and User logins for 15 minutes (LoginLockoutMinutes).

Password History Window

5pw / 24pw

5 / 24

PasswordHistoryCount defaults to 5 previous $s2$ hashes and clamps per tenant up to 24.

Breached Password Denylist

8616entries / 10000entries

8616 / 10000

Embedded NFKC lowercase wordlist checked by BreachedPasswordChecker on password set and reset.

How Do Next.js 16 MVVM, ASP.NET Core 33-Stage Middleware, and Identity Services Connect?

Diagram structure
  • Next.js Edge Proxy fe_edge
  • RouteGuard & MVVM fe_guard
  • 401 Mutex & Factory fe_api
  • Pipeline Stages 17-25 edge_mw
  • Auth Controllers ctrl_auth
  • Policy & $s2$ Hasher policy_svc
  • Session & Revocation session_svc
  • Identity Schema DB id_store
  • fe_edge → fe_guard · cookie + headers
  • fe_guard → fe_api · memory JWT + sudo
  • fe_api → edge_mw · Bearer + HttpOnly
  • edge_mw → ctrl_auth · authorized
  • ctrl_auth → policy_svc · verify & check policy
  • ctrl_auth → session_svc · issue / revoke tokens
  • policy_svc → id_store · PasswordHistory + Otp
  • session_svc → id_store · RefreshToken + Audit

Client requests cross Next.js 16 Edge routing and fail-closed middleware gates before reaching SessionIssuerService and Identity persistence. Click any linked child diagram to inspect the dedicated backend workflow, session lifecycle, physical schema, or frontend MVVM implementation.

  1. Next.js Edge Proxy ↗

    Evaluates scr_auth_state hint cookie, APP_ROUTE_MANIFEST, and isSafeRedirectTarget while enforcing strict next.config.ts CSP and WebAuthn headers.

  2. RouteGuard & MVVM ↗

    Keeps accessToken in memory-only useAppStore, exempts recovery routes, orders PendingPayment -> mcp -> mfa_enroll, and blocks SignalR until clear.

  3. 401 Mutex & Factory ↗

    Shares activeRefreshHandler, activeLogoutHandler, withCredentials: true, and tenant headers across all per-module ApiService clients via api-factory.ts.

  4. Pipeline Stages 17-25 ↗

    Validates scripe_iat_ms (+5ms), jti, and imp in OnTokenValidated, then runs ApiKeyUsage, post-auth rate limits, TrustedCidr, MustChangePassword, and RequireMfaEnrollment.

  5. Auth Controllers ↗

    Enforces fail-closed tenant ID decryption (422), [AllowAnonymous] /user/logout, password-policy & force-change-password parity, and 410 Gone on /external-logins/link.

  6. Policy & $s2$ Hasher ↗

    Verifies $s2$ SHA-256 pre-hashed BCrypt (work factor 12), 8,616 denylist entries, PasswordHistory, and Verification:VerifierKey HMAC OTPs.

  7. Session & Revocation ↗

    Enforces TwoFactorPendingToken (5m), TwoFactorAttemptLockHelper, immutable AbsoluteExpiresAt (24h / >=30d / 8h imp), and MaxConcurrentSessions.

  8. Identity Schema DB ↗

    Persists RefreshTokens, PasswordHistories, PasswordResetTokens (varchar(64) hash), OtpCodes, and admin_security_profiles with zero plaintext secrets.

3

How Does Non-Auto-Login Password Recovery Interact With Session Issuance and Revocation?

Password recovery separates OTP validation from password mutation, revokes all active sessions atomically, and requires a clean sign-in afterward.

Diagram structure
  • Browser / Recovery UI user
  • AdminAuth / UserAuth ctrl
  • Otp & Reset Store otp
  • Session & Revocation rev
  • user → ctrl · POST request-password-reset
  • ctrl → user · 202 Accepted (uniform)
  • user → ctrl · POST verify-reset-otp (code/token)
  • ctrl → otp · Check HMAC / SHA-256 hash
  • otp → user · 200 workspaces + policy + ResetGrantToken
  • user → ctrl · POST reset-password (ResetGrantToken)
  • ctrl → rev · Mutate $s2$ + PasswordHistory + Revoke all
  • rev → user · 204 No Content (no tokens issued)
  • user → ctrl · POST login (fresh credentials)
  • ctrl → rev · Issue Session + scripe_iat_ms + JTI

Why Reset Password Returns 204 Without Auto-Login

Returning 204 No Content eliminates post-reset session fixation, preserves MustChangePassword and RequireMfaEnrollment wall ordering, and forces fresh MFA evaluation (TwoFactorPendingToken) on the next login.
